official.description_text:
Doctoral student in fusion plasma physics and nuclear engineering
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Electrical Engineering
The provision of plasma-facing components (PFCs) with sufficient lifetime is one of the major technological obstacles to be overcome in developing fusion reactors. Recently, the damage of PFCs due to interaction with runaway electrons (RE) has become a highly critical issue in evaluations of disruption consequences.
ITER
, currently seeks for the validation of relevant numerical models and tools against existing experimental evidence in order to gain confidence in their applications to predictive reactor modelling.
PhD project will focus on the development of modelling tools for simulations of RE-induced PFC damage and their validation against data from
EUROfusion Consortium
, and
DIII-D (USA)
. The validated models will be employed for predictive modelling of specific ITER scenarios following input from the ITER Organization. The modelling of MeV RE energy deposition in PFCs will be performed with Monte Carlo simulations. These results will serve as input for the thermomechanical models to be developed in FEM and CFD software to address severe deformation and potential explosion of the material.
We offer expertise in the theory and modelling of plasma-surface interactions and electron transport into matter, access to state-of-the-art experimental data from the largest tokamaks worldwide and close collaboration with the Experiments & Plasma Operation Section of the ITER Organization.
Supervision:
Prof. S. Ratynskaia. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
Programming skills in languages such as Fortran, Python, or C/C++,  is required for this position.
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work,
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach,
analyze and work with complex issues,
demonstrate familiarity with the modelling of electron transport into matter with Monte Carlo techniques (i.e. GEANT4, PENELOPE, FLUKA etc.
demonstrate familiarity with basic computational fluid dynamics techniques and
demonstrate familiarity with basic computational solid mechanics techniques.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement
. Read more about
Doctoral studies (PhD) | KTH | Sweden
.

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages. Copies of originals must be
certified
.
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

For

If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: Doctoral position in fusion plasma physics focusing on runaway-electron-induced damage to plasma-facing components in ITER tokamaks. Work involves Monte Carlo simulations (electron transport), thermomechanical FEM/CFD modelling, and validation against experimental data from large fusion facilities.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position is physics/nuclear engineering (fusion plasma, runaway electrons, PFC damage, reactor modelling). Researcher's themes are human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, collaborative interaction, and wayfinding. Zero connection.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both involve computational modelling and experimental validation, but contexts and techniques are entirely different. Position requires Monte Carlo simulations (GEANT4, PENELOPE, FLUKA), FEM/CFD thermomechanical modelling, and fusion physics expertise. Researcher's methods are HCI user studies and immersive system evaluation. No meaningful methodological transfer.

growth_value.rationale: Would not advance target identity or close capability gaps. Researcher's gaps are in HCI evaluation depth (eye-tracking, physiological sensing, mixed-effects modelling), collaborative XR design, and spatial cognition theory. Fusion physics and Monte Carlo simulations offer no leverage toward those goals.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is well-regarded technical university in Sweden (target geography, priority country). Access to ITER collaboration and EUROfusion Consortium represents high-level research infrastructure. However, fusion plasma physics is orthogonal to researcher's strategic domain. Supervision (Prof. Ratynskaia, plasma-surface interactions) is unrelated to XR/HCI. Prestige and infrastructure do not offset fundamental domain misalignment. Additionally, posting hints at possible security clearance requirements, which may introduce complexity.

eligibility_flags: Position requires 'programming skills in languages such as Fortran, Python, or C/C++.' Researcher has advanced C# (Unity), intermediate Python (beginner, no substantial project experience), but no documented Fortran or C++ experience. Partial eligibility on Python but weak.

Position requires 'familiarity with modelling of electron transport into matter with Monte Carlo techniques (GEANT4, PENELOPE, FLUKA).' Researcher has zero documented Monte Carlo or particle-transport simulation experience.
Position requires 'familiarity with basic computational fluid dynamics techniques and computational solid mechanics techniques.' Researcher has no documented CFD or FEM background.

Position may be classified as security-sensitive under Swedish Protective Security Act (2018:585), triggering security clearance requirement. Researcher's non-EU background (Malaysia) may introduce delays or complications.

Admission requires Master's (or equivalent 240+ credits with 60+ second-cycle). Researcher has MSc by Research in-progress, still in thesis stage — may not yet hold completed degree at application/admission time.
risks: Fundamental domain barrier: fusion plasma physics requires deep prior coursework in physics, plasma theory, and computational methods. Researcher's background is design/multimedia.
Research domain orthogonal to target identity: runaway electron damage in tokamaks has no connection to XR, HCI, spatial cognition, or immersive learning.
Severe skill gaps: Monte Carlo simulations (GEANT4/PENELOPE), CFD, FEM, and plasma physics theory. Ramp-up would be substantial and delay doctoral research progress.
Supervision orthogonal: Prof. Ratynskaia's expertise (plasma-surface interactions, electron transport) is in physics; no overlap with immersive systems or HCI.
Possible security clearance requirement (Swedish Protective Security Act) may introduce bureaucratic delays or barriers for non-EU applicant.
Four-year commitment in fusion physics would significantly delay PhD pathway in target domain.
